newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran official says Berlin verdict "politcal show".
newsitem.headline: Iran official says Berlin verdict "politcal show".

text.p: Iran on Friday stepped up its attacks against a German court ruling which accused Tehran of ordering the murders of dissidents in Berlin, branding it a political show without legal value.
Deputy Foreign Minister Mohammad Javad Zarif said the verdict was "nothing but a political show" because the Berlin court had failed to follow accepted legal procedures.

The official Iranian news agency IRNA said Zarif blasted the court, which he said "solely relied on remarks of a number of terrorists and hijackers, for whose arrest warrants have been issued by the Iranian judiciary".

"These elements are members of the counter-revolutionary groups, whose aim is to mar the prestige of Iran. From a legal point of view, statements of these people lack any legal credibility. No legal decision could be made on these remarks," said Zarif, who is in charge of legal and international affairs at the ministry.

Zarif was referring to the court's use of testimonies by Iranian opposition members including Abolhassan Banisadr -- Iran's first president who fled to France after being deposed in 1981. Tehran accuses Banisadr of hijacking and other crimes.
The Berlin court on Thursday said Iran's political leadership ordered the killings of an Iranian Kurdish dissident leader and three aides in Berlin's Mykonos restaurant in 1992.

It avoided names but said the assassinations were ordered by a secret special operations committee whose members included Iran's president, religious leader, intelligence minister and head of foreign policy.
Iran has repeatedly denied all responsibility for the killings which it blames on infighting among opposition groups.
The ruling has sparked an international diplomatic row, with Germany, Sweden and Australia recalling their ambassadors from Iran and the EU inviting other members to join the action.
Tehran also withdrew its envoy from Bonn and expelled four German diplomats after Germany asked four Iranian diplomatic staff to leave.
Germany has been Iran's largest trading partner and most important Western friend.
Zarif accused the court of not giving the defence the right to voice its views.

"The remarks of the Berlin court judge lack any legal value on the ground that they are merely based on the statements and allegations levelled by the said people (counter-revolutionaries) against Iran, who lack competence, but also because the court has failed to provide the defendant with an equal right for defence," Zarif said.
IRNA said Iran's ambassador to Bonn had written a letter to the judge two years ago saying he was ready to provide evidence refuting the allegations made against Iran, but never got a reply.
The court gave life sentences to Kazem Darabi, an Iranian, and Abbas Rhayel, a Lebanese. Two other Lebanese received prison sentences of between five and 11 years as accomplices.
It found a fifth man innocent of complicity charges.
